title: ADMIN says a nick is on no server of mimid's; WHOIS says it is on this one
description:
Found by the spec review of branch irc-verbs.

Session::admin (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/command.rs) answers 402
ERR_NOSUCHSERVER for any target that is not `*`, the configured server
name, the asking user's own nick or SERVICE_NICK. Its doc comment gives
the reason: "every other nick this front end knows belongs to someone at
a provider, who is connected to no server of mimid's".

Session::whois in the same file says the opposite, sending
312 <nick> <this server> :mimid-agent for every user nick it knows.

Modern §"ADMIN message": "If <target> is a client, the information for
the server that client is connected to is requested", and reserves
ERR_NOSUCHSERVER for when "a matching server cannot be found" -- which,
by mimid's own 312, it can. So WHOIS bob-b and ADMIN bob-b give a client
two incompatible answers about where bob-b is.

Two ways out:
- Accept any nick this run has given (Names::user_of returning Some) as
  naming this server, which is exactly the set WHOIS answers 312 for,
  and keep 402 for a name that is neither this server nor a nick here.
- Or keep the behaviour and fix the stated reason: say ADMIN matches no
  client target at all, and add that to the crate's # Limitations beside
  the wildcard entry, so the two numerics' disagreement is on the record
  rather than contradicted by a comment.

Decision mimid-1wgh.142 carries ADMIN's readings and should gain
whichever is chosen. The crate's # Limitations records only the wildcard
deviation today.
